steps.text: Gather the ingredients. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Lightly grease a 7x11-inch casserole dish.

Layer sliced squash, zucchini, onion, and tomatoes in the baking dish, sprinkling with cheese and adding pats of butter between each layer of vegetables, and seasoning with salt and ground black pepper to taste. Continue layering process until vegetables are used up; top with remaining butter and cheese.
Cover the casserole and bake in the preheated oven until vegetables are to desired tenderness and cheese is melted and bubbly, about 20 to 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Squash and Zucchini Casserole
raw_recipe.description: A squash and zucchini casserole with layers of sliced yellow squash, zucchini, onion, tomato, and cheese baked until bubbly for a tasty veggie side.

review.reviewBody: This is a very delicious dish. I have made it twice. The first time I made it, I followed the instructions and layered the squash, zuchinni, onion, and tomatoes. Then I read the "pats of butter between each layer" part. Too late to do that. So the second time I made this I kept that in mind. I also did not slice the zuchinni lenthwise the second time, and it was much easier to eat with them sliced as regular slices.

I didn’t cover the casserole when baking, hoping that some of the liquid released from the veggies would cook off, but there still was a puddle in the bottom of the dish. And that wasn’t a game changer for me, I just poured it off when serving. I really thought this amount of Romano would be too much. But no, it adds GREAT flavor. Pecorino-Romano doesn’t really melt, so if you’re looking for that, you’ll have to add another melting cheese like cheddar, Swiss, Gruyere, or mozzarella. However, I felt there was enough cheesy flavor in this casserole. If you’re looking for fresh flavor from garden veggies that are in abundance right now, you won’t be disappointed…I wasn’t.
Topped with panko, used olive oil sprinkled on instead of pats of butter, and added fresh basil. Excellent! Thanks for the recipe.

To prevent having too much water, salt the squash and zucchini heavily and allow to sit for 30 minutes, then rinse. It takes out much of the excess water. Also, be sure to seed the tomatoes. Finally, I like to add a little tomato paste to the mixture to thicken.

I really like this casserole with all the fresh veggies. I browned chicken breast in a skillet and layered it on the bottom of the pan before the vegetable. I also sprinkle just a bit of Chachere's. I will make this again.

My entire family raved about this dish! I also used fresh veggies from farmer's market and followed a few other suggestions, sliced the veggies in the round, used mozzarella cheese and put one package uncooked minute rice in the bottom of baking dish. The rice suggestion was meant to absorb juice overflow, which it did, but my family enjoyed the rice with the dish! I enjoyed the leftovers 2 days later! This one will be a family dinner staple!

I dislike when people rate a recipe based on the changes they have made, so first of all as is I think that this recipe is quite good, definitely 3 1/2 stars. With a few small changes I think it can get even better. I tried this recipe for the first time today. I added a few tablespoons of breadcrumbs as recommended by another reviewer to give it a little crunch, this was definitely a good decision. I also added a tiny bit of garlic salt on top of the bread crumbs as I felt it needed just a tiny bit more flavor. I think next time I might make a few small changes. I was thinking about sauting a little garlic in the butter and brushing that on the layered zuchinni and squash. I also think that a little fresh basil might taste nice as for some reason this reminds me of a light pizza. Overall this is a great, simple recipe that offers everyone a good starting point and something to build off of!

Made this according to recipe, except I used a shredded 4 cheese pizza package I had on hand, and added about 1/2 cup dry grated parmesan cheese on top. Also used a combination of Vidalia and red onions. Baked it uncovered. It was still incredibly juicy with a crispy crunchy topping, but great over a black/brown rice combination. Very delicious! Added a bit of garlic powder after cooking. Would also add fresh basil next time. It was fantastic! Will definitely make again!

Very tasty recipe! I followed the suggestions of a few other reviewers and did not cover it and it came out great. I also did not have any fresh tomatos so I used canned with basil and oregano and also put bread crumbs on top which made the top layer extra crunchy! Everyone was pleasantly surprised and liked it even those who say they don't like zucchini or squash. Will definitely make it again!

This casserole came out yummy and smelled so good when I took it out. The only change I made was to sprinkle a bit of shredded cheddar on top because I ran short on parmesan between the layers and covered it with foil for the first 20 mins. I took the foil off for the last 10 mins and let it get brown and bubbly. Kids ate it all up!

This was a delicious way of preparing veggies! It tasted fresh and yummy, even with "winter" tomatoes and squash. I used Mexican gray squash because I had them on hand. I cut the squash into lengthwise slices and halved the slices. I also layered in four sliced mild mini peppers. After 30 minutes of baking, the top of the casserole was golden, and the squash was cooked tender yet still retaining a bit of firmness. In addition to salt and pepper, I sprinkled in Herbes de Provence and garlic powder. In the future, I may try adding Trader Joe’s Aglio Olio seasoning instead of garlic powder and Herbes de Provence. Overall, a great, easy-to-follow recipe!

I made it and it was really delicious. I did not have fresh tomatoes on hand, so I used several sliced canned whole tomatoes. The only change I plan to make is to use just a little more pepper to season next time.
WOW!! Amazing! Absolutely delicious ~ the whole crew LOVED it!! Thank you for sharing!
Added a bit of garlic powder, diced red bell pepper, and a bit of shredded mozzarella pepper jack cheese on top. Wonderful!
Excellent! Also added cubed ham and veggie mix had leftover. Garlic butter ansd cheddar sheese in addition. Will make again! Put on pellet grill for 1 hr.
It was delicious
I followed the recipe exactly. My family and I loved it, simple, fresh and delicious.

This is the best way to serve squash and zucchini to kids! My granddaughter didn't like the sound of it until she took a bite, it was all over after that. It is now one of her favorites. The one thing I did change was that I buttered my dish instead of oil and I used an Italian cheese blend for the topping. If you haven't tried this one, you really should!

Delicious I am making it again. I did make a few changes but stayed with the basic used mozzarella ,quesadilla and coby cheese i love cheese. I season layer by layer. I read several of the made it recipes and followed some of there tips. It did produce a lot of juice so I made a pot of steam rice and the juice made more flavorful. will make again

Absolutely delicious! I had fresh zucchini, butternut squash, and tomatoes from the garden and I was worried because sometimes the zucchini peel is bitter, and the squash too hard, but everything came out just perfect. I just cooked everything for about 50 minutes, rather than 30 minutes. Thank you, yummy!
